title: Erased subprotocol agrees off the reachable region
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over Alice's inputs $X$ and Bob's inputs $Y$, let $s$ be a rooted subprotocol of $p$ recorded by a subprotocol path from $s$ to $p$, and let $p'$ be the protocol obtained from $p$ by collapsing the subtree $s$ to a single leaf carrying the canonical output of $s$ (its leftmost leaf value). Suppose an input pair $(x,y)$, with $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$, does not reach $s$: it fails to be consistent with all of Alice's and Bob's branch choices along the path from the root of $p$ down to the root of $s$. Then running $p'$ on $(x,y)$ produces the same output as running $p$ on $(x,y)$.
hypotheses_covered: a subprotocol path witnessing that s is a rooted subtree of p
the input pair (x,y) does not reach s (fails reachesPath, i.e. is inconsistent with the choices along the path)
replaced:
If $(x, y)$ does not reach the subprotocol path \texttt{hsp}, then running the erased
protocol \texttt{erasePath hsp} on $(x, y)$ gives the same output as running $p$.
